journey.name: Discover — global browse, topics, people, search
journey.description:
Discover with ZERO follows is the point of this journey (#26): a brand-new account must see real decks and real people without knowing anyone's pubky. Everything below the header comes from the Nexus indexer, so it needs a signed-in session (journey 01) and at least one deck published network-wide with a topical tag — journey 02 produces exactly that.
If the indexer has not ingested anything yet, the browse strip shows "Nothing published here yet" with a "Search people & decks" CTA. That is a pass for the empty case, not a failure: verify the honest empty state rather than skipping the journey. Confirm which case you are in with `curl 'https://nexus.staging.pubky.app/v0/stream/resources?app=loopky&tags=loopky-deck&limit=5'` before starting.
**The empty block and the error block are different screens and this journey checks both** (#321). "Nothing published here yet" is a claim about the network and may only appear after the indexer has actually answered; an unreachable one shows "You're offline" with a Retry. Browse also pages now, so the count that curl reports is the number to hold the screen to — not the first screenful.

actions.action: Launch the Loopky app and verify the Home screen is shown
Tap the element with resource-id "tab_discover" in the bottom tab bar
Verify the Discover screen is shown (resource-id: discover_screen) with a search button (resource-id: discover_search) in the header — a magnifier, not the old "Add friend" pill
Verify a "Browse decks" section is present — this is the global browse, and it must NOT require following anyone

Wait for the browse strip to settle, then verify EITHER at least one deck tile (resource-id: discover_deck_tile) OR the empty block (resource-id: discover_browse_empty) reading "Nothing published here yet" with a "Search people & decks" button (resource-id: discover_browse_empty_search). There must never be a bare "Follow a friend to see their decks here" dead end.

Verify every deck tile's cover follows ONE rule: the picture runs the full width of its tile, corner to corner, with no strip of the tile's own surface down either side. Square and portrait covers are the ones that break this (#255), so check a grid holding both those and a landscape cover — the defect is the inconsistency between neighbours, not the inset alone.

Count the indexed decks first: `curl -s 'https://nexus.staging.pubky.app/v0/stream/resources?app=loopky&tags=loopky-deck&sorting=timeline&limit=100&skip=0' | jq length`. Scroll the browse grid to its end, counting distinct deck titles, and verify the screen reaches that number rather than stopping at the first page (#321). Before paging, Discover showed 11 of 71 on staging and nothing reached the rest.
While scrolling, verify each new page appends UNDER the decks already on screen — the grid must never blank and re-populate, and your scroll position must not jump
Scroll to the end of the browse grid and verify the last row's title and "N cards · author" line clear the floating tab bar and can be read
If a topic chip row is visible (resource-id: discover_topic_row), tap the first chip (resource-id: discover_topic_chip)

Verify the browse heading changes to "Decks tagged “…”" and a "Clear" control appears (resource-id: discover_clear_tag). The deck list is re-queried from the indexer, so it may legitimately differ from the unfiltered list.

Verify the chip row narrowed: the chosen chip leads, and every other chip is a tag some deck in the filtered grid also carries — a chip no such deck carries must be gone, since tapping it would find nothing

Tap a second chip (resource-id: discover_topic_chip) and verify BOTH stay selected, the heading reads "Decks tagged “first” + “second”", and every tile in the grid carries both tags — several topics are an AND, never an OR. Check one tile against `curl -s 'https://nexus.staging.pubky.app/v0/resource/by-uri?limit_tags=100&limit_taggers=1&uri=…'` rather than trusting the stream, which cuts each resource's tag list at five

Tap every remaining unselected chip in turn, tapping it again to drop it, and verify none of them lands on the "No deck carries all of these tags yet" block — that is the promise the narrowed row makes
Tap the FIRST chosen chip again and verify only that tag is dropped: the other stays selected and the heading returns to a single "Decks tagged “…”"
Tap the element with resource-id "discover_clear_tag" and verify every chip is deselected, the full topic row returns, and the heading reads "Browse decks"
If a "People on Loopky" strip is visible (resource-id: discover_people_row), tap the Follow pill on the first person (resource-id: discover_follow) and verify it flips to "Following" immediately
Pull to refresh and verify the followed person no longer appears in the People strip — suggestions exclude people you already follow
Note: the People strip is legitimately absent when the only published decks are your own, since suggestions exclude yourself. That is a pass.
Tap the element with resource-id "discover_search"

Verify the search screen opens (resource-id: search_screen) with the keyboard already up on the input (resource-id: search_input), a scan button (resource-id: search_scan) and the hint "Search by name, or paste a pubky…" (resource-id: search_hint)

Type the first few letters of a known Loopky display name and wait ~1s WITHOUT typing further. Verify one search runs after the pause rather than one per keystroke: a spinner (resource-id: search_loading) appears once, then a "People" section with rows (resource-id: search_person) and/or a "Decks" section (resource-id: search_deck_tile).
Verify each person row carries a Follow pill; tap it and verify it flips to "Following" immediately
Type nonsense that cannot match ("zzzqqqx") and verify the no-matches block (resource-id: search_empty) reading “Nothing found for …”, not a blank screen
Clear the box with the element with resource-id "search_clear" and verify the hint returns
Type your OWN pubky into the field with resource-id "search_input"
Verify a direct-hit row appears immediately (resource-id: search_direct_hit) reading "Open this profile" — an address needs no index, so it must NOT wait for the debounce or the network
Tap the element with resource-id "search_direct_hit"
Verify your own profile is shown with NO Follow button (regression: you could follow yourself)
Navigate back to Discover

Turn the device radios off, pull to refresh, and verify the screen still renders: BOTH the "From people you follow" section and the "Discover decks" section show "You're offline" with a working Retry. The screen must never go blank — and browse must NEVER show "Nothing published here yet" here, which is the #321 bug: a claim about the network from a device that never reached it.
Tap the Retry under "Discover decks" with the radios still off and verify it fails again honestly — same message, no spinner left running, no empty state
Turn the radios back on, tap that same Retry, and verify the browse grid fills without needing a pull-to-refresh

Turn the radios off again mid-scroll, scroll to the foot of the browse grid, and verify the decks already loaded STAY on screen with an error and Retry under them — a failed page is a footer that could not load, not a strip that could not load. Turn the radios back on, tap that Retry, and verify the next page appends below the decks already there with no duplicates.
